description:
The same 555 LED blinker as the perfboard example, on stripboard: the strips run across the board and do most of the wiring, with a few links and cuts. Laid out the way the Learn guides suggest: https://perfboarddesigner.com/learn/stripboard-layout/

**Strips.** From the top: +9 V, ground, the LED's strip, the chip's four rows, the timing strip and ground again.

**Power in.** A 9 V battery clip plugs into J1 on the left, + at the top. D2 (1N4001) lies along the top strip across a cut, so current can only reach the circuit the right way round. C3 (100 µF) and C4 (100 nF) sit across the two supply strips.

**The chip.** U1 straddles four cuts, one under each pair of facing pins, so every pin has a strip of its own. Red links take U1.8 and U1.4 (reset) to +9 V, black links take U1.1 to both ground strips, and yellow links join U1.2 and U1.6 on the timing strip.

**Timing.** R1 (1 kΩ), R2 (68 kΩ) and C1 (10 µF) make the LED flash about once a second. C2 (10 nF) keeps U1.5 quiet.

**Output.** R3 (470 Ω) feeds D1 from U1.3, at about 10 mA.

**Mounting.** The corners are kept clear for M3 screws, a row away from any strip in use.
